node.title: Re: Perl substitute with the nth match
node.author: choroba
node.doctext:
> OF COURSE I can do this in a loop. Or with a /e

Can you? I can, too:

perl -pe 's/cat/++$i/ge' file

There's no special variable that counts matches. But there's one that's incremented with each line of input: [doc://perlvar#$.]. So if we could tell Perl that cat instead of a newline is the line delimiter... but of course we can do that! That's what [doc://perlvar#$/] is for.

perl -pe 'BEGIN { $/ = "cat" } chomp; $_ .= $. unless eof' file

Update: which can be rewritten to use substitution as you originally wanted: perl -pe 'BEGIN { $/ = "cat" } s{$/}{$.}' file
